scientific_use: Prepare gene-level, unnormalized RNA-seq counts and sample metadata as a DESeqDataSet suitable for negative-binomial modeling. Align count-matrix columns exactly to metadata rows, encode condition/type as factors, specify ~ condition, and optionally filter genes with counts >=10 in at least the smallest group size.

The vignette stresses raw/un-normalized counts; normalized/transformed values are not model input. Optional prefilter is an example choice, not a mandatory DESeq2 requirement.
outputs: DESeqDataSet with counts, column metadata and design ~ condition; optional subset retaining rows passing the stated count rule. Feature names are row names; a following example adds them redundantly to row metadata.

title: Estimate gene-wise and fitted mean-dispersion relationships

sources.locator: usage, fit types, value and estimation details; lines 1-103
Dispersion plot and fitting alternatives; lines 1972-2020

scientific_use: Estimate gene-specific negative-binomial dispersions, fit their mean relationship and return MAP estimates used for downstream differential testing and the variance stabilizing transformation.
tool_role_basis: Calls DESeq2's existing estimateDispersions implementation; this inventory records its documented use, not method creation.
inputs: A DESeqDataSet with counts, sample design and size factors or normalization factors. Fit options are parametric, local, mean, or glmGamPoi; method choice affects the fitted trend and downstream estimates.
outputs: DESeqDataSet with gene-wise/trended/final dispersion estimates in row metadata and final dispersions accessible through dispersions(). The fit trend is also used by VST.
dependencies: Estimated size factors or normalization factors
evidence: estimateDispersions.Rd lines 1-85 specifies fit choices and the sequence of profile-likelihood estimate, trend and MAP estimate
Rmd lines 1972-2020 demonstrates diagnostic plot and custom-fit alternative
limitations: No dispersions were estimated or plotted.
Choice of trend family and outlier handling is data-dependent; source inspection does not validate the fit for a new dataset.
glmGamPoi-specific execution and compatibility were not tested.

title: Inspect per-sample count concentration and sparsity

sources.locator: full manual; lines 1-34

scientific_use: Visualize how each sample's counts are concentrated across genes as a diagnostic for highly sparse matrices with a few large counts that may be poorly represented by a negative-binomial model.
tool_role_basis: Uses the existing plotSparsity diagnostic; no modeling or plotting method is implemented.
inputs: A count matrix or DESeqDataSet; optionally normalized counts. The manual example generates a simulated dataset and estimates size factors before plotting.
outputs: A diagnostic plot of sample count concentration; this is not an inferential test or a direct measure of biological sparsity.
evidence: plotSparsity.Rd lines 1-34 defines the input and explains the intended diagnostic and simulated example
limitations: The source says the plot is not technically the same as sparsity and describes it as a useful diagnostic only.
No plot or count distribution was inspected; do not treat it as validation of a negative-binomial model.

title: Form contrasts and genotype-specific condition effects

sources.locator: Contrasts and Interactions; lines 1487-1623; chunks simpleContrast and combineFactors; also extended coefficient reparameterization lines 1799-1836

scientific_use: Estimate pairwise level comparisons as linear combinations of GLM coefficients, or test whether a treatment effect differs across genotype using combined-factor or interaction designs.
tool_role_basis: Uses DESeq2's existing design and results APIs to extract scientifically chosen effects; no model-fitting implementation is changed.
inputs: Fitted count model plus a factor design with adequate samples per combination. A simple factor contrast is contrast=c('condition','C','B'); interaction example uses genotype, condition and their interaction. The source recommends a combined factor for many questions and explains that the main condition coefficient under an interaction design is the effect at the reference genotype.
outputs: A DESeqResults table for a pairwise contrast, a named coefficient, or difference of coefficients; interactions quantify how a condition effect differs from the reference genotype.
dependencies: Sample-level condition/genotype metadata and an identifiable fitted design
evidence: Rmd lines 1487-1513 defines pairwise factor contrasts and linear-combination forms
Rmd lines 1514-1623 explains combined factor versus interaction and coefficient interpretation
Rmd lines 1799-1836 shows reference-level changes that turn contrasts into coefficients for shrinkage
limitations: Examples are generic and mostly eval=FALSE; no study-specific count matrix is supplied.
Coefficient meanings depend on factor reference levels and design-matrix coding.
Complex contrasts should be checked against the actual resultsNames and estimable design.
